value.title: PR 229 executable lifetime repair verified at 324a47f

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Closure of the previous "Atomic executable replacement preserves code but not current_exe path lifetime" note: #229 P229-F001 is fixed at 324a47fe0d086c442a7607f0aecd48323acb12ad. Round 2 passed with the Defender deploy prerequisite retained.

The installer compares bytes and leaves an identical installed inode untouched. For changed installs, usable_observer_executable preserves a valid literal current_exe pathname, otherwise accepts the suffix-free installed file when Linux reports " (deleted)". The daemon calls this helper before constructing the child-observer command.

The live-process regression copies the executable, runs it, renames a fresh inode over it, then requires the still-running process to exec its usable observer path successfully. Linux additionally asserts the raw deleted-path precondition and failed raw exec. This replaces the original proof ceiling: hard-link content survival alone was not a later-exec guarantee.

CI run 42934405272, successful-job JUnit artifact 13817922147, individually records all six F187 cases executed and passed. No reviewer-local build/test/install ran under Jordan's one-build-per-PR ruling. The canonical round-2 verdict carries the detailed closure; the old block note is historical, not an open finding.

Defender's installed-copy process exclusion remains an admin-confirmed deploy prerequisite, not something a green spawn count or Linux CI proves.
